title: Joual basics: common contractions
goal: By the end of this lesson you can recognise the most common contractions of casual Quebec speech (chu, t'sé, y'é, a l'a, y'a, j'vas, pis, ben) and map each one back to standard French.

body: *Joual* (from a casual pronunciation of *cheval*) is the name given to the popular, working-class French of Montreal. Writers like Michel Tremblay put it on stage in the 1960s and made it a symbol of Quebec identity.
Today, people often use 'joual' loosely for any very casual Quebec speech. Some find the word negative, so many linguists prefer *français québécois familier* (informal Quebec French).

Your goal this lesson is to understand it, not necessarily to speak it. Everyone uses some contractions (*chu*, *t'sé*, *pis*); heavier forms (*moé*, *toé*, *icitte*) sound rural, old-fashioned or very informal.

The biggest changes happen to subject pronouns before *être* and *avoir*. *Il* becomes *y*, *elle* becomes *a* (and *a l'* before a vowel), *je suis* becomes *chu*, and *tu* loses its *u* before a vowel.
learn.tip: y = il / ils, a = elle. Most of joual is just pronouns squeezed together.

body: *Tu sais* → *t'sé* (you know), used as a filler in almost every sentence. *Je ne sais pas* → *j'sais pas* → *chais pas* or *ché pas*.
*Puis* → *pis* (and, and then). *Bien* → *ben* (very, well). *Là* at the end of a sentence adds emphasis: *Viens icitte, là!*
*Je vais* → *j'vas*, or *m'as* for a near future: *M'as te dire une affaire* (Let me tell you something). *Sur la* → *su'a*, *dans la* → *dans'a*: *C'est su'a table* (It's on the table).
*Moi*, *toi* → *moé*, *toé* (older or very informal). *Ici* → *icitte* (rural or very informal).

Spoken Quebec French turns a statement into a yes/no question by adding *-tu* after the verb, with any subject: *T'as-tu faim?* (Are you hungry?), *C'est-tu loin?* (Is it far?), *Y vient-tu?* (Is he coming?).
This *tu* has nothing to do with 'you'. In writing, use *est-ce que* or inversion: *Est-ce que c'est loin?*

quebec.intro: This whole week is the Quebec layer: the contractions t'sé, y'é, a l'a and chu that the roadmap lists are all accurate and extremely common. Understand them all; use the light ones (chu, t'sé, pis) with friends, and keep standard forms for writing and formal situations.

items.note: Informal; the l' links a and a

drills.why: It turns the sentence into a question; it doesn't mean 'you'.
y'a = il y a; ben du monde = beaucoup de gens.

drills.q: Which is the most acceptable in a job interview?
drills.why: Use standard forms in formal situations.

drills.q: Standard: Mes clés sont ___ table. (spoken: su'a)
drills.en: My keys are on the table.

drills.q: Standard: Je vais au café, ___ je reviens. (spoken: pis)
drills.en: I'm going to the café, then I'll come back.

drills.why: chais pas / j'sais pas in speech.

a: Il y a beaucoup de monde.
Il y a beaucoup de gens.
Il y a bien du monde.
drills.why: y'a ben du monde in speech.

vocab.en: he is, it is (= il est)
there is / he has (= il y a / il a)
I don't know (= je ne sais pas)

pron.tip: SHU: one syllable for je suis.
ta-tsu FAN, rising at the end.

dialogue.fr: Non, chu chez nous. Pis toi?
dialogue.en: No, I'm at home. And you?

dialogue.fr: Chu au dep. T'sé, Julie, ta voisine? A l'a eu son bébé!
dialogue.en: I'm at the corner store. You know Julie, your neighbour? She had her baby!

dialogue.fr: Ben voyons! C'est-tu un gars ou une fille?
dialogue.en: No way! Is it a boy or a girl?

dialogue.fr: Une fille. A'est ben belle, y paraît.
dialogue.en: A girl. She's really beautiful, apparently.
And her boyfriend, where is he?

dialogue.fr: Chais pas, y travaille à soir, je pense.
dialogue.en: I don't know, he's working tonight, I think.

dialogue.fr: M'as y apporter un cadeau demain.
dialogue.en: I'm gonna bring her a gift tomorrow.

dialogue.fr: Bonne idée! Bon, faut que j'y aille. Bye!
dialogue.en: Good idea! OK, I have to go. Bye!

speak.prompt: Translate into standard French: 'Chu fatigué, pis y fait frette.'
speak.model: Je suis fatigué, et il fait très froid.

speak.prompt: Translate into casual Quebec speech: 'Elle a faim. Est-ce que tu as faim?'
Say three sentences about your day using chu, t'sé and pis.
speak.model: Chu allé au travail à matin, pis j'ai dîné avec mes collègues. C'était le fun, t'sé.

write.prompt: Rewrite this casual text message in standard French: 'Salut! Chu en retard, y'a ben du trafic. T'sé, a l'a pas appelé. Tu viens-tu à soir? M'as t'attendre au resto.'
write.model: Salut! Je suis en retard, il y a beaucoup de circulation. Tu sais, elle n'a pas appelé. Est-ce que tu viens ce soir? Je vais t'attendre au restaurant.

options: Let me tell you / I'm gonna tell you

quiz.q: Which is the standard form of 'Y'en a pus'?
quiz.why: Y'en a pus = Il n'y en a plus.

quiz.q: Which form sounds the most old-fashioned or rural?
quiz.why: Moé, toé, icitte are older or very informal.
